facts.statement: The genus Franconiasaurus contains only one known species, F. brevispinus, which is known from two well-preserved three-dimensional skeletons.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, F. brevispinus, known from two well-preserved three-dimensional skeletons.

facts.statement: Fossils of Franconiasaurus were discovered in the Mistelgau fossil pit in the Bayreuth District of Bavaria, Germany.
facts.quote: The Franconiasaurus fossil material was discovered in sediments of the Mistelgau fossil pit of the lower Jurensismergel Formation (Grammoceras thouarsense Zone) in Bayreuth District, Bavaria, Germany.

facts.statement: Franconiasaurus brevispinus was formally described as a new genus and species in 2024 by Sachs, Eggmaier, and Madzia.
facts.quote: In 2024, Sachs, Eggmaier & Madzia described Franconiasaurus brevispinus as a new genus and species of plesiosauroid based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The genus name Franconiasaurus combines the region of Franconia with the Greek word for reptile.
facts.quote: The generic name, "'Franconiasaurus", combines Franconia, after the Bavarian region of the type locality, with the Greek "σαῦρος" ("sauros"), meaning "reptile".

facts.statement: The species name brevispinus refers to the short neural spines found on some of its cervical and dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The specific name, "brevispinus", references the short neural spines of some of the cervical and dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Franconiasaurus as a member of Plesiosauria that is the sister taxon to Cryptoclidia.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, Sachs, Eggmaier & Madzia (2024) recovered Franconiasaurus as a plesiosauroid member of the Plesiosauria, as the sister taxon to the Cryptoclidia.

facts.statement: Franconiasaurus is considered to fill an evolutionary gap between early plesiosauroids and later-diverging groups like cryptoclidids and elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: This suggests that Franconiasaurus fills an evolutionary gap between more basal taxa (like early plesiosauroids including Plesiosaurus-like forms and microcleidids) and later-diverging taxa (including cryptoclidids, leptocleidians, and elasmosaurids).

facts.statement: Franconiasaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period in Germany.
facts.quote: Franconiasaurus (meaning "Franconia reptile") is an extinct genus of basal plesiosauroid plesiosaurs from the Early Jurassic of Germany.

facts.statement: Franconiasaurus lived between 180.4 and 174.7 million years ago during the Toarcian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (180.4 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Franconiasaurus brevispinus is the only known species of the extinct genus, a basal plesiosauroid plesiosaur from the Early Jurassic of Germany.
facts.quote: Franconiasaurus brevispinus (que significa "reptil de Franconia de espinas bajas") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Franconiasaurus un plesiosaurio plesiosauroideo basal del Jurásico Inferior de Alemania.

facts.statement: The animal is known from two well-preserved three-dimensional skeletons.
facts.quote: Conocido por dos esqueletos tridimensionales bien conservados.

facts.statement: Fossil material was found in the Mistelgau fossil pit within the lower Jurensismergel Formation in the Bayreuth District of Bavaria, Germany.
facts.quote: El material fósil de Franconiasaurus fue descubierto en sedimentos del pozo fósil de Mistelgau de la Formación Jurensismergel inferior (Zona Grammoceras Thouarsense) en el distrito de Bayreuth, Baviera, Alemania.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen BT 011224.00 was discovered between 2014 and 2018 and consists of a nearly complete, partially articulated skeleton.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, BT 011224.00, fue descubierto entre 2014 y 2018 y consta de un esqueleto casi completo y parcialmente articulado.

facts.statement: An incomplete, disarticulated specimen discovered in 2005 was also referred to Franconiasaurus.
facts.quote: BT 011241.00, un espécimen desarticulado incompleto descubierto en 2005, también fue referido a Franconiasaurus.

facts.statement: Paleontologists Sachs, Eggmaier, and Madzia described Franconiasaurus brevispinus as a new genus and species in 2024.
facts.quote: En 2024, los paleontólogos Sachs, Eggmaier y Madzia describieron a Franconiasaurus brevispinus como un nuevo género y especie de plesiosauroide basado en estos restos fósiles.

facts.statement: The generic name combines the region of Franconia with the Greek word for reptile.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico, "'Franoniasaurus", combina la palabra Franconia, en honor a la región bávara de la localidad tipo, con el griego "σαῦρος" ("sauros"), que significa "reptil".

facts.statement: The specific name brevispinus refers to the short neural spines on some of the cervical and dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: El nombre específico, "brevispinus", hace referencia a las cortas espinas neurales de algunas de las vértebras cervicales y dorsales.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses define Franconiasaurus as a plesiosauroid member of Plesiosauria and the sister taxon to Cryptoclidia.
facts.quote: En sus análisis filogenéticos, Sachs, Eggmaier y Madzia (2024) definieron a Franconiasaurus como un miembro plesiosauroide de Plesiosauria, como taxón hermano de Cryptoclidia.

facts.statement: Franconiasaurus is suggested to fill an evolutionary gap between basal plesiosauroids and later-diverging taxa such as cryptoclidids and elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: Esto sugiere que Franconiasaurus llena una brecha entre taxones más basales (como los primeros plesiosauroides, incluidas las formas similares a Plesiosaurus y microcleididos) y taxones divergentes posteriores (incluidos criptoclidios, leptocleidianos y elasmosáuridos).
